subsystems.name: Motor
subsystems.role: converts electrical current into high-speed rotary motion with high torque density.

subsystems.name: Gearbox
subsystems.role: reduces motor speed and multiplies torque while preserving backdrivability.

subsystems.name: Sensing
subsystems.role: measures joint position and motor current for closed-loop control.

subsystems.name: Control electronics
subsystems.role: drives the motor with field-oriented control and implements torque, velocity and impedance loops.

subsystems.name: Housing and bearings
subsystems.role: provides structural support, heat dissipation and precise alignment.

buildSteps.title: Design the motor
buildSteps.detail: Choose pole count, winding pattern and air gap to balance torque density against iron losses and heat.

buildSteps.title: Wind the stator
buildSteps.detail: Copper wire is wound into slots, then impregnated with varnish to hold it in place and improve heat transfer.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the rotor
buildSteps.detail: Permanent magnets are glued or sleeved onto the rotor, which is then balanced for high-speed operation.

buildSteps.title: Cut and harden gears
buildSteps.detail: Planetary gears are machined from alloy steel, heat-treated, and ground to precise tolerances.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the gearbox
buildSteps.detail: The motor shaft is coupled to the sun gear, planets are placed in the carrier, and backlash is set with shims.

buildSteps.title: Install sensors
buildSteps.detail: Encoders are mounted on motor and output shafts to measure position and allow torque estimation.

buildSteps.title: Integrate electronics
buildSteps.detail: A driver board is attached or connected remotely, flashed with firmware that runs current, velocity and impedance loops.

buildSteps.title: Test and calibrate
buildSteps.detail: The actuator is run on a dynamometer to map torque, efficiency, backdrivability and thermal limits.

prerequisites.why: high torque density requires strong neodymium-iron-boron magnets.
low-ratio planetary gears must be accurate to minimise vibration, backlash and wear.
field-oriented control at high frequency is needed for smooth, responsive torque.
joint torque is often inferred from current or strain gauges, but accurate low-cost sensors are still improving.
motors can overheat during continuous high-torque work, so cooling paths must be designed in.

pathway.milestone: quasi-direct drive actuators are used in research quadrupeds and some commercial humanoids
pathway.unlocks: dynamic running, jumping and compliant interaction.

pathway.milestone: integrated joint modules combine motor, gearbox, encoder and driver in one sealed unit
pathway.unlocks: faster robot assembly and lower cost.

pathway.milestone: higher torque density through advanced cooling and magnet materials
pathway.unlocks: stronger limbs for heavy lifting and more powerful locomotion.

pathway.milestone: mass-produced actuators with lifetime and safety certification
